primitives.asks: Is the fix the holder's to perform?

branches.label: Holder can re-authorise
branches.test: the cause is a withdrawn, expired or insufficient authorization on the holder's side of the connection

branches.label: Not theirs
branches.test: the cause is a provider outage, a defect on our side, or an entitlement the holder does not control

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it

primitives.purpose: Say which capabilities have stopped and that nothing is required from them, with no reconnection step attached - because there is no step that would work.
primitives.brief: Say which capabilities have stopped and that nothing is required from them, with no reconnection step attached - because there is no step that would work. Prompting a re-auth against a provider outage produces a person who tries three times and then opens a ticket
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.state: informed, recovery not the holder's to perform
primitives.reEntry: if the cause is later reclassified as holder-fixable, this qualifies again on the re-authorisation path

primitives.asks: How much of the connection is affected?

branches.label: Some capabilities
branches.test: the authorization still covers part of what was granted and the rest of the connection keeps running

branches.label: Nothing works
branches.test: no capability on this connection can run until it is re-authorised

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Name exactly which capabilities stopped, which are still running, and the single re-authorisation step.
primitives.brief: Name exactly which capabilities stopped, which are still running, and the single re-authorisation step. Telling somebody their whole connection is broken when most of it works buys an afternoon of unnecessary work and a lasting distrust of the next notice

mustNotClaim: a reduced authorisation as a full one

primitives.brief: Say the connection is carrying nothing at present, name what has stopped depending on it, and give the single re-authorisation step. What stopped is the part the holder needs in order to judge how urgent this is
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.purpose: Confirm which capabilities are working again and name any that came back reduced.
primitives.brief: Confirm which capabilities are working again and name any that came back reduced. A reconnection that silently restores less than before is discovered later, at whatever moment the missing capability was needed
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.reEntry: a later break on the same connection is a new instance

primitives.state: connection deliberately removed by the holder

primitives.does: Record that the recovery window closed with the connection still broken, as a dated fact about this integration rather than a conclusion about the relationship. A connection somebody chose not to restore is one signal, and it may be the deliberate end of a use case rather than a customer leaving

primitives.asks: Is there independent evidence that the relationship itself is at risk?

branches.label: Corroborated
branches.test: risk evidence from another source already exists against this relationship, so the unreconnected integration adds to a picture rather than being the whole of it

branches.label: This break is the only signal
branches.test: nothing else indicates the relationship is at risk

primitives.state: recovery window closed, connection still broken, relationship not labelled at risk
primitives.reEntry: a further disconnection event, or a re-authorisation attempt, opens recovery again

primitives.on: a connection the holder could re-authorise and has not, past the point where the break is still being treated as an interruption
carries: which capabilities have been unavailable and for how long
what was already said about the break and on which routes
